title: Adaptive Pool Command Center — compact controls for Dedicated GPU pools
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Design a compact, action-first UI surface for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces health, autoscale controls, and burst settings in a single command center. Goal is to reduce time-to-action for operators and platform engineers: identify pool anomalies, adjust autoscale policies, and trigger/limit burst capacity without navigating to multiple screens.

Scope: UI patterns for a single-line pool summary, expandable controls (quick actions + advanced flyout), health sparkline, cost impact preview for adjustments, and small device responsive behavior. Includes: Figma prototype, interaction spec, accessibility checks, and a short usability test with two SREs.

Out of scope: billing admin workflows, long-form logs, full incident timelines (kept on separate Fleet Ops page). This is focused on operational controls and quick diagnostics only.
acceptance_criteria: Single-line pool row shows: pool name, utilization %, health indicator, effective autoscale state, current burst allowance, and quick-action menu.
Clicking 'Adjust Autoscale' opens an inline flyout with target min/max GPU counts, scale-sensitivity slider, and an estimated cost delta shown before save.
Burst controls allow immediate 'Request burst' and 'Throttle burst' with confirmation; UI shows remaining burst budget and last burst timestamp.
Health sparkline shows last 1h and 24h toggle; hovering reveals bucketed percentiles and recent alerts.
Prototype passes accessibility audit for color contrast and keyboard-only interactions for all controls.
Design handoff includes tokens, spacing, and microcopy; engineering signoff obtained on interaction timing and API contract links.
research_notes: Interviewed 3 platform SREs: priority is immediate visibility of burst budget and ability to revert autoscale changes quickly.
Observed common flow: identify high tail latency -> check pool utilization -> increase burst or tighten autoscale thresholds.
Competitive scan: other vendors separate health dashboard and controls; operators prefer co-located controls for incident mitigation.
Usability test plan: 5 tasks, measures: time-to-adjust, confidence score; to run with 4 internal participants next week.
